newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London steady, eye Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London steady, eye Wall Street.

text.p: Japanese shares traded in London were slightly higher in early afternoon, but nervously watching developments on Wall Street, traders said.
"Japan has recoupled itself with New York in the past month or two with worries about interest rates and the possibility of U.S. investors liquidating their positions," said one.
U.S. investors have shifted from being buyers of Japan to neutral, to small sellers of the market, said the trader.
With the Dow falling over 50 points as strong economic data reinforced fears about higher interest rates, traders in London warned the Nikkei could break below 20,000 on Monday.
"We've been slightly nervous to indifferent all day and I think we're biased to the slightly nervous at the moment but New York is difficult to call and it could close 20 points higher," he said.
By 1419 GMT the Nikkei 50 was up just 2.44 points at 1,378.72.
In Tokyo overnight, the Nikkei 225 tumbled nearly two percent, extending its losses for a third straight day. The index finished over 386 points lower at 20,166.90.
